description: From children struggling with their mental health to adults worried about AI, many of us feel neglected and ignored by politicians. As if the world’s problems are too big, or politicians too small, to get a grip on everything from rising prices to emergent threats such as AI? If so, says the political strategist Claire Ainsley, you’re neither alone nor irrational. “It’s probably because you’ve got a lot to do, and the world is out of control,” she says cheerfully from her home in York, where she lives with her husband, an artist, and their two teenage children. Sillars’ new party was a media sensation in Scotland, and quickly joined by public intellectuals such as Tom Nairn , Hamish Henderson and Neal Ascherson . It offered something new and exciting: a fusion of the two movements that were battling for Scotland’s soul in a decade that had already been defined by electoral clashes between Labour and the Scottish National party.

As the affordability crisis rages on, people may feel some relief at the small cost of living measures announced for households and businesses. But when we’ve been told we’ll get a wholesale reset and an end to neoliberalism, 4p off the price of gherkins and a temporary tiny bank tax isn’t going to cut it.

description: Lyn Dade and Lyn Collins respond to an article by John Humphrys about the 1966 disaster and the lessons that haven’t be learned John Humphrys’ righteous anger at the carelessness of national institutions and the horrors that followed as a result – at Aberfan, Hillsborough, Grenfell and during Covid – is matched only by his disgust at the lack of accountability afterwards ( At Aberfan, I saw fathers digging for their missing children. And the lessons society should have learned, it hasn’t, 24 October ). Sadly, it is too often true that those in leadership roles walk away with no more than a slapped wrist. In France, citizens would be manning the barricades. Here? “Dreadful, isn’t it?” Followed by a shrug. Like Humphrys, we should be raging at the death, grief and lasting trauma that were delivered by our “leaders”. But we don’t. Because we don’t believe that it will make any difference. We are apathetic, maybe because we have so little self-agency.

Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. description: Jacob Morley, a convicted killer on the loose since Sunday, has no known connection to the small Illinois town where the truck he is accused of stealing was found, the police chief said Wednesday. “What we have seen kind of leads us in the direction that he’s not still here. But that doesn’t mean that we’ve stopped looking,” Marion Police Chief David Fitts said. Morley, 28, convicted of killing a co-worker in 2022 , was serving a life sentence when he escaped from Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, sometime before 11:30 p.m. Sunday, officials there said. Morley had stolen a work truck, and early Tuesday that truck was found behind a business in Marion, a town of around 16,000 that is around 100 miles north of Tiptonville, authorities in Marion and Tennessee said. title: Judge rebuffs Trump DoJ’s bid to force California to set aside 20,000 ballots
author: Sam Levine
categories: US midterm elections 2026 | US news | US politics | World news | US voting rights | California | West Coast
description: Justice department had demanded state segregate and not count ballots from people it claimed were non-citizens A federal judge declined to order California election officials to segregate and not count ballots from people the Trump administration claimed were non-citizens, rebuffing a legally thin request from the justice department that appeared designed to cast doubt over the results of the midterms. The ruling from US district judge David Carter, nominated to the federal bench by Bill Clinton, comes about two weeks after the justice department delivered a USB drive to election officials in Los Angeles and Sacramento that it said contained the names of 20,000 non-citizens on the state’s voter rolls. There are more than 23 million registered voters in California and non-citizen voting is extremely rare .
